page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8559C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and backed by a large 320 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, providing a generous 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 5000 GB NVMe SSD, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps under the Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the i7ie.2xlarge demonstrates strong single-core performance, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2312.0 and a top-tier text processing score of 2963.0. Single-threaded operations are highly efficient, with gzip compression reaching 34.73 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.03 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Its DDR5 memory subsystem yields a strong Passmark memory score, though large uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks sit in the average range at 63.39 GB/sec and 58.36 GB/sec respectively.

The hardware profile offers high resource density, combining substantial local NVMe storage with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. This makes it highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring rapid access to large local datasets without the overhead of network-attached storage. However, multi-core scaling and complex tasks like 7B LLM text generation represent a performance tradeoff, with the latter registering a weaker 6.9 tokens/sec. The instance is best suited for storage-heavy and database workloads, transactional databases, caching layers, and data-intensive applications.
